items.title: Section: A Balance Scale's Perfect Simultaneity — How "Severing All Three Times" Actually Works

items.zh: 答：非斷去來今，然說斷三世。何以故？若在過去有隨眠心，任運滅故，其性已斷，復何所斷。若在未來有隨眠心，性未生故，體既是無，當何所斷。若在現在有隨眠心，此剎那後，性必不住，更何須斷。又有隨眠離隨眠心二不和合，是故現在亦非所斷。然從他音、內正作意二因緣故，正見相應。隨所治惑，能治心生，諸有隨眠所治心滅。此心生時，彼心滅時，平等平等，對治生滅道理應知。正見相應能對治心，於現在世無有隨眠，於過去世亦無隨眠；此剎那後離隨眠心，在未來世亦無隨眠。從此已後，於已轉依、已斷隨眠身相續中，所有後得世間所攝善、無記心去來今位，皆離隨眠，是故三世皆得說斷。是名煩惱雜染染淨差別。云何建立煩惱雜染迷斷差別？
items.en: Answer: it is not the past, future, or present that is severed, yet it is said that all three times are severed. Why? A past mind bearing latent tendency has already ceased of itself, its nature already ended — what more is there to sever? A future mind bearing latent tendency has not yet arisen, its nature not yet existing — what is there to sever? A present mind bearing latent tendency, this very moment not enduring beyond itself, needs no severing either. Also, a mind bearing latent tendency and a mind free of latent tendency cannot coexist, and so the present too is not what is severed. Yet through hearing from another and correct inward reflection, a mind corresponding to right view arises. As the antidote-mind arises corresponding to whatever affliction is being countered, the mind bearing that very latent tendency ceases. This arising and that ceasing occur with perfect simultaneity — the principle of antidote's arising and ceasing should be understood this way. This is the defiled-and-pure distinction of affliction defilement.

items.title: Section: Fifteen Latent Tendencies Across Three Realms and Four Truths

items.zh: 當知略說有十五種。謂欲界繫，見苦集滅道諦所斷，及修所斷，諸漏有五。如欲界繫，色無色繫各五亦爾。欲界迷苦有十煩惱。迷集有八，除薩迦耶及邊執見。如迷集諦，滅、道亦爾。上界諸諦並除瞋恚。隨迷次第，如欲界說。
items.en: It should be known that, in summary, there are fifteen kinds. Those bound to the desire realm, severed by seeing the truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path, together with those severed by cultivation, number five with their outflows. As with the desire realm, the form realm and formless realm each likewise contribute five. In the desire realm, delusion about suffering has ten afflictions. Delusion about origination has eight, excluding self-view and extreme-view. As with delusion about origination, so too with cessation and the path. In the upper realms, every truth further excludes hatred. The order of delusion follows as stated for the desire realm.

items.title: Section: Self-View's Twenty Modes, and the Heretics Who Denied Suffering Itself

items.zh: 略五取蘊總名為苦。愚夫於此五取蘊中，起二十句薩迦耶見。五句見我，餘見我所。是名迷苦薩迦耶見。即用如是薩迦耶見以為依止，於五取蘊見我斷常，故邊執見亦迷於苦。又諸邪見，謂無施等，乃至妙行、惡行業果及與異熟，是迷苦諦。又有邪見，撥無父母、化生有情，如是邪見一分迷苦、一分迷集。又諸外道誹謗苦諦，起大邪見。彼謂沙門喬答摩種，為諸弟子施設苦諦，此定無有。如是邪見亦迷苦諦。
items.en: In brief, the five clinging-aggregates together are called suffering. The ignorant, with respect to these five clinging-aggregates, generate twenty modes of self-view. Five modes see the self; the rest see what belongs to the self. This is called delusion about suffering through self-view. Taking this very self-view as its foundation, seeing the self as annihilated or eternal with respect to the five clinging-aggregates, extreme-view too is delusion about suffering. Also, various wrong views hold that there is no giving, and so on, up to no virtuous or unwholesome karmic fruit or its ripening — this is delusion about the truth of suffering. There is also a wrong view that denies parents and spontaneously-born beings; such a wrong view is in part delusion about suffering and in part delusion about origination. Also, certain heretics slander the truth of suffering, giving rise to great wrong views. They claim that the ascetic of the Gautama clan established the truth of suffering for his disciples, and that it certainly does not exist. Such a wrong view is likewise delusion about the truth of suffering.

items.title: Section: Eternalist Gods, the Edge of the World, and Eel-Wriggling Evasion

items.zh: 又有諸見，妄計自在、世主、釋、梵及餘物類，為常、為恒，無有變易。如是邪見亦迷苦諦。又有諸見計邊、無邊，如是亦名迷苦邪見。又有沙門、若婆羅門不死矯亂邪見一分，亦迷苦諦。若有見取，妄取迷苦所有諸見以為第一，謂能清淨、解脫、出離，如是名為迷苦見取。若有妄取隨順此見，此見隨法所受戒禁，以為第一，能得清淨、解脫、出離，此戒禁取，是迷苦諦。
items.en: There are also views that falsely compute a lord of self-mastery, a sovereign of the world, Indra, Brahmā, and other such kinds as permanent, eternal, and without change — such wrong views are also delusion about the truth of suffering. There are also views computing an edge or no edge — these too are called wrong views of delusion about suffering. There is also a portion of eel-wriggling wrong view arising among ascetics or brahmins, which is likewise delusion about suffering. If there is view-attachment, falsely grasping whatever views belong to delusion about suffering as foremost, as able to purify, liberate, and release, this is called view-attachment through delusion about suffering. If one falsely grasps, in accordance with such a view, whatever precepts and vows follow from that view, as foremost, as able to attain purification, liberation, and release, this precept-attachment is delusion about the truth of suffering.

items.title: Section: Closing the Ten Roots of Delusion About Suffering

items.zh: 若有外道於此諸見不定信受，亦不一向誹謗如來所立苦諦，但於苦諦心懷猶豫，此及所餘於苦猶豫，是迷苦疑。若於如是自所起見寶愛堅著，如此見貪，是迷苦貪。若於異分他所起見，心懷違損，是迷苦恚。若恃此見，心生高舉，是迷苦慢。若有無智，與此諸見及疑、貪等煩惱相應，若唯於苦獨行無智，如是並名迷苦無明。此十煩惱皆迷苦諦，見苦所斷。云何迷集有八隨眠？謂諸沙門、若婆羅門謗因邪見。又有沙門、若婆羅門，計自在等是一切物生者、化者及與作者，此惡因論所有邪見。
items.en: If some heretic does not firmly accept these views, nor outright slanders the truth of suffering established by the Tathāgata, but merely wavers in mind regarding the truth of suffering, this and any other wavering about suffering is doubt through delusion about suffering. Treasuring and firmly clinging to views one has oneself generated is greed through delusion about suffering. Wishing to oppose or harm another whose views differ is hatred through delusion about suffering. Relying on such a view and generating an elevated, arrogant mind is conceit through delusion about suffering. Lacking wisdom, whether associated with these views, doubt, greed, and so forth, or acting alone solely with respect to suffering, is together called ignorance through delusion about suffering. These ten afflictions are all delusion about the truth of suffering, severed at the path of seeing. How does delusion about origination have eight latent afflictions? Certain ascetics or brahmins hold the wrong view denying any cause. There are also ascetics or brahmins who compute a lord of self-mastery or the like as the producer, transformer, and maker of all things — this too is a wrong view belonging to the evil-cause theory.

items.zh: 又有邪見，無施、無愛，亦無祠祀，無有妙行，亦無惡行。又有邪見，不死矯亂外道沙門、若婆羅門所起一分。

blocks.text: What exactly is severed when affliction is severed? Not the past, which is gone, nor the future, which is not yet; the seeds, at one moment, like a scale tipping.
Master Cháng Bǎi: it is not the seeds of three times that are severed. The arising of the curing wisdom and the ceasing of what it cures happen at once, like the two ends of a scale.
Master Cháng Bǎi: afflictions cut at seeing are of four kinds (by the four truths), those cut by cultivation one; across three realms, fifteen.
Master Cháng Bǎi: clinging to form, feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness as self gives the modes of self-view. Some heretics deny that suffering exists at all.

Master Cháng Bǎi: they do not know that even gods' aggregates are impermanent, suffering, empty, and without self. (Ru-Yi's heading also mentions the "eel-wriggling" evaders who never commit to an answer.)

subs.head: Ten roots of delusion about suffering

blocks.text: These are cut at the path of seeing. (Untranslated, 0624a18: further wrong views denying giving, sacrifice, and good and bad conduct; and part of the "eel-wriggling" of some ascetics.)
The scale image is precise: wisdom rises and affliction falls in the same instant. Severing is not a slow scraping away but a moment of seeing.

quiz.q: The English §31 opens with "Answer:" What was dropped, and what is the effect?
options: it drops the question whether past, future, or present is severed, leaving the answer unanchored; a later passage is missing too
nothing: the question at §30 is the one answered here, so that the two sections form one exchange, as the lecture's outline confirms, with nothing missing
the word 答 is missing
"Why" is added
quiz.why: The treatise first asks whether what is severed is past, future, or present; the Chinese and English here start only from the answer. Master Cháng Bǎi: it is not the seeds of the three times that are severed, yet severing the three times is provisionally spoken of. Without the question the answer has nothing to attach to.

quiz.q: Why is a mind with latent tendency in none of the three times what is severed?
options: past latency has ripened; future latency is repented
all three times are unconditioned
latent tendency does not exist
the past has ceased; the future has not arisen; the present does not last and cannot join the free mind
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the mind with seeds ceases of itself, its nature gone; the mind with latency and the mind free of it are of different natures and cannot join, and so the present is not severed either. The argument leads to the next point about simultaneous arising and ceasing.

quiz.q: What does 平等平等 mean?
options: equal regard for all beings, friend and foe, and the two minds having equal rank, unrelated to any question of simultaneity, as the lecture explains
the arising of curing wisdom and ceasing of latency are simultaneous, like a balance's two ends
vision and cultivation have equal merit
the afflictions of the three times are equal in number
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the arising of the curing wisdom and the ceasing of what is cured are simultaneous; this is 平等平等. By ultimate principle, severing seeds is not severing the three times. The English "perfect simultaneity" renders it well.

options: ten in desire, three in form, two in the formless
ten root and five secondary afflictions
five per realm: four severed by seeing the truths, one by cultivation
five views and ten non-views
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: conceptual afflictions severed at vision are of four kinds, and innate ones severed by cultivation count as one, making five. With three realms that makes fifteen. The English "number five with their outflows" is awkward: the five are the outflows.

quiz.q: How many afflictions delude about each truth in the desire realm, and which are excluded?
options: ten about suffering; eight each about the others, excluding self-view and extreme view
eight about suffering; ten about origin; seven each about the rest, excluding greed and conceit, delusion about the cause being worse
ten for every truth
eight for every truth
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the desire realm's afflictions deluded about origin are eight, without self-view and extreme view. As §33 shows, these two arise directly on the five clinging-aggregates, which are the truth of suffering, and so they count only there.

quiz.q: What are the upper realms' counts, and why?
options: the upper realms have none
ten and eight, the same as the desire realm
five and three
hatred is excluded: nine about suffering, seven about each other truth
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: there are nine about suffering, and seven about origin, and seven each about cessation and the path; beings of the form and formless realms are deluded about the truths in the same way, except for hatred. The English is clear here.

quiz.q: How are the twenty modes of self-view divided?
options: five see a self; the remaining fifteen see what belongs to self
ten see a self and ten what belongs to it, each aggregate having two sides, the former being heavier, and all belonging only to outsiders
five of permanence, fifteen of annihilation
five of the desire realm, fifteen above
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: clinging to form, feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness as self makes the five modes of self-view; the ordinary five aggregates come from affliction, craving, and grasping, and are called clinging-aggregates. The rest, fifteen, see what belongs to self.

quiz.q: The English has "merely for his disciples." What is the problem with "merely"?
options: no problem: their claim is that it is a mere device for disciples
the problem is "Gautama," which should be "Śākya"
"merely" is added and shifts the claim: they say it does not exist, not that it was only for disciples
the problem is "truth," which should be "fact"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the establishing of the truth of suffering for the disciples — this certainly does not hold. The point of the heretic is that it does not exist. "Merely," absent in the Chinese, suggests it exists for disciples alone. The same formula recurs for origination at §36, without "merely."

quiz.q: Why does denying parents and spontaneous beings count partly under suffering and partly under origin?
options: denying parents is unfilial, leading to suffering next life, and the evil karma is origin, an explanation by result, unrelated to parents' own nature
parents are ripened bodies, suffering by nature; as causes of children it is delusion about origin
parents belong to cessation
parents belong to the path
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: parents themselves are of the nature of suffering, being ripened bodies made of the five aggregates, and so it is delusion about suffering; as the causal ground producing sons and daughters it is delusion about origin. The same object has both sides.

quiz.q: Why is holding Īśvara, Indra, and Brahmā permanent a delusion about suffering?
options: not knowing gods' clinging-aggregates too are impermanent, suffering, empty, without self
because they think gods create all, creation being origin
because gods have severed suffering
because gods belong to cessation
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: they do not know that even gods' clinging-aggregates are impermanent, suffering, empty, and without self. At §35, by contrast, holding such a god to be the maker of all things is delusion about origin, the difference being between the god as enduring and as cause.

quiz.q: The English has "severed at the path of seeing." Compared with §36, what is uneven?
options: nothing uneven: both belong to the path of seeing, §36 wrongly adding "origination," the lecture saying all is severed at once without division by truth
it drops 十
it drops 煩惱
it drops 苦: §36 has "seeing origination," and the division by truth disappears
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi explains these as severed at the path of vision, called 見苦所斷. Since §32 counts the outflows by the four truths seen, the object 苦 matters. §36 translates "severed at the path of seeing origination," so §35 should parallel it with "seeing suffering."
